recent_articles.title: Scientists used AI and high-tech scans in Peru’s Nazca Desert; the result was 303 hidden geoglyphs
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Researchers** from **Yamagata University** and **IBM Research** used artificial intelligence (AI) to analyze high-resolution satellite images of the Nazca Pampa, identifying 303 new relief geoglyphs.  The AI model, which analyzed existing data at speeds 20 times faster than human experts, identified these hidden figures in just half a year, nearly doubling the known catalogue. The newly discovered geoglyphs depict human shapes, domesticated animals, and severed heads, suggesting they may have been used for rituals or territorial boundaries within local communities. This breakthrough technology also offers valuable insights into the lives of the Nazca people who created them over 2,000 years ago and provides a digital record that can be used to protect these sites from threats like urban sprawl and mining activities.

recent_articles.title: Bay system to trigger wet spell, ease heat in Tamil Nadu for next few days - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC)** has issued a yellow alert for heavy rainfall in several districts of Tamil Nadu, including Villupuram, Mayiladuthurai, Cuddalore, and Theni on Saturday.  **D.S. Pai**, Head of the RMC, Chennai, stated that the well-marked low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal will persist for the next few days, bringing relief from the heat with moderate rainfall expected across the state until May 19th.  The weather system is also expected to improve conditions for the advancement of the Southwest monsoon over parts of south Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.

recent_articles.title: 10 countries with highest anaconda population in the world: From Brazil to French Guiana
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Anacondas**, known for their preference for water environments, are found in various wetland regions across northern and central South America. **Brazil** boasts the largest population due to its vast Amazon rainforest and Pantanal wetlands. Other countries with significant populations include **Venezuela**, **Colombia**, **Bolivia**, **Peru**, **Ecuador**, **Paraguay**, **Guyana**, **Suriname**, and **French Guiana**.  These snakes are typically found in flooded grasslands, jungle rivers, marshes, and remote areas where human activity is limited.

recent_articles.title: Monsoon to reach Kerala on May 26, says IMD - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts the southwest monsoon will advance into Kerala on May 26, a day earlier than its usual June 1 arrival.  While this year's monsoon onset is anticipated to be early, there are concerns about below-normal rainfall. The IMD has historically been accurate in predicting the monsoon's arrival over Kerala, with only one exception in 2015. **M. Ravichandran**, Secretary of the Ministry of Earth Sciences, stated that after the monsoon onset, a period of heavy rain is expected for the next five days.  The IMD has warned of potential drought impacts due to reduced rainfall and the ongoing El Nino phenomenon.

recent_articles.title: 15-year-old Canadian boy built a robotic turtle that can detect underwater environmental threats with 96% accuracy
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Evan Budz**, a 15-year-old from Dundas, Ontario, developed the Bionic Underwater Robotic Turtle (BURT) to monitor delicate aquatic areas.  The invention incorporates biomimicry by mimicking snapping turtles' swimming movements and features high-quality cameras and machine-learning models for detecting invasive species and coral bleaching with a 96% accuracy rate. **Evan Budz** showcased BURT at the European Union Contest for Young Scientists (EUCYS) where it was recognized for its potential impact on large-scale ecological monitoring.  The project demonstrates how student-driven innovations can contribute to environmental protection.

recent_articles.title: DMRC rolls out hydrogen buses in Central Vista - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC)**, in collaboration with the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs** and the **Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas**, launched a hydrogen-powered shuttle bus service in Delhi's Central Vista area on May 15, 2026. The service, which will operate during peak office hours from Monday to Friday, aims to promote green hydrogen as a clean fuel alternative and strengthen environment-friendly public transport solutions. **Dr. Amit Kumar Jain**, DMRC Director (Operations and Services), received the ceremonial keys of the buses from **Arvind Kumar**, **Indian Oil Corporation** Director (Refinery).

recent_articles.title: Weather tracker: Furnace Creek sizzles as snow sweeps Siberia in a week of extremes | Environment | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Honduras**, **North America**, and **Indonesia** experienced record-breaking temperatures this week, with **Choluteca**, Honduras, setting a new all-time May maximum temperature record.  In the western US, Furnace Creek recorded 46.7C, while **Bali airport** in Indonesia set a new overnight heat record of 27.9C.  Meanwhile, **China** saw extreme weather conditions ranging from high temperatures to violent storms and heavy snowfall.

recent_articles.title: Britons to vote in inaugural contest to find nation’s favourite butterfly | Butterflies | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Butterfly Conservation** is hosting a poll to determine Britain's favorite butterfly. The charity, which has previously seen success with the Big Butterfly Count and other similar initiatives, hopes this contest will reveal which of the 60 native species holds the most affection for the nation.  The poll runs until June 7th and includes contenders such as the purple emperor, small copper, small tortoiseshell, large blue, and swallowtail. The results will crown Britain's favorite butterfly.

recent_articles.title: 370 billion crickets farmed every year may actually feel pain, shocking new study suggests
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A new study in the journal *Proceedings of the Royal Society B* challenges the long-held belief that crickets are simply reacting to stimuli. Researchers observed house crickets exhibiting "flexible self-protection" by repeatedly grooming injured limbs, suggesting a more complex processing of pain than previously thought. This discovery raises ethical concerns about the welfare of 370 billion crickets raised annually for food and prompts calls for humane killing methods and improved living conditions.  The study highlights the need to address the regulatory vacuum surrounding invertebrate sentience, as most animal welfare laws exclude invertebrates.

recent_articles.title: US miner under further investigation after destroying WA habitat of black cockatoos, quokkas and numbats | Western Australia | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Alcoa**, a US mining company, is facing further investigation into its clearing of jarrah forest in Western Australia. The ongoing inquiry follows the company's "deliberate repeat breach" of environmental laws that destroyed habitat for protected species and resulted in a $40 million settlement to avoid prosecution.  The federal government labeled Alcoa's clearing as a "deliberate repeat breach," while the company maintains its operations have been conducted in accordance with WA legislation. The investigation into potential illegal clearing at Alcoa's Willowdale mine is ongoing, adding pressure on the company's bauxite mining in southwest WA, which threatens Perth's water supply and has destroyed about 280 sq km of jarrah forest.

recent_articles.title: Australia’s housing affordability expected to worsen and homelessness soar under fossil-fuelled future | Housing | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **University of Sydney** researchers found that global heating could worsen housing affordability, leading to increased rents and a quadrupling of homelessness in Australia by 2036.  Their study, which modeled the housing market under different climate scenarios, showed that vulnerable households would be disproportionately affected under a fossil-fuelled future. The research highlights the need for fairer housing policies that prioritize support for renters on low incomes and address homelessness. **Associate Prof Nader Naderpajouh** from the University of Sydney emphasized the importance of tailoring interventions to specific needs while acknowledging the urgency of addressing climate change in housing policy.  Economist **Nicki Hutley**, a Climate Council councillor, called for prioritizing climate considerations in housing policies, including emissions reduction and resilience measures.

recent_articles.title: Forest dept. seeks speedy ro-ro ferry access for snake rescuers in Kochi - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kerala Forest department** has requested the **Kochi Corporation** to expedite access for snake rescue volunteers to the Vypeen–Fort Kochi ro-ro ferry service. The request, made by the Deputy Conservator of Forest, seeks special permission for direct entry into the service due to the emergency nature of their work.  The application will be considered at the next **Corporation Council** meeting. Rescued snakes are transported to shelters or the Social Forestry department in Edappally.

recent_articles.title: Unseasonal storms leave 111 dead in Uttar Pradesh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: At least 111 people were killed and hundreds more injured in **Uttar Pradesh** after a powerful storm brought heavy rain, strong winds, and thunderstorms.  The **U.P. Relief Commissioner’s office** reported damage to homes, trees, and electric poles across 26 districts. **Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath** directed officials to provide aid to victims and release compensation. **Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav** called for comprehensive relief efforts and urged the government to assess losses and ensure insurance payments.

recent_articles.title: River Thames in London gets first official bathing spot on Friday | Water | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Environment Agency** has designated 13 new bathing water areas across England, including the River Thames at Ham in London.  This designation follows years of campaigning by groups like **Teddington Bluetits**, who sought to improve water quality and increase public access to swimming spots. The new sites will be monitored weekly throughout the summer season for pollution levels, with the goal of reducing sewage discharge from water companies. **Emma Hardy**, the Water Minister, emphasized the government's commitment to improving water quality in rivers and boosting tourism.

recent_articles.title: Hidden beneath Oklahoma’s white salt flats lies a crystal found nowhere else on Earth that people can dig up for free
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Great Salt Plains in Oklahoma are home to a rare geological treasure: hourglass selenite crystals. These transparent, sand-and-clay-filled crystals have distinctive hourglass patterns and are only found in this specific region of the United States. Visitors can legally dig for the crystals themselves within designated public areas, turning the remote salt flats into a popular tourist attraction. The site is also home to important wildlife habitats and offers visitors a chance to experience a unique combination of geology, history, and natural beauty.

recent_articles.title: One dead, several injured in landslide in Jamuria coal mines in West Bengal; many feared missing - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A landslide at the Kunustoria Padashiya Colliery in West Bengal's Jamuria coal belt on Thursday, May 14, 2026, resulted in one fatality and multiple injuries. **Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL)** workers were trapped inside the collapsed mine after an air blast during blasting operations.  Rescue efforts are ongoing, with injured workers being treated at local hospitals. Local residents and union leaders have demanded fair compensation for the deceased and injured workers.

recent_articles.title: FIFA warned ‘gruelling heat’ could impact a quarter of World Cup games | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **FIFA** has been warned by **World Weather Attribution (WWA)** that one in four World Cup games could be played in very hot conditions due to global warming.  Climate experts estimate 26 matches will reach a temperature of at least 26C, with 17 playing in stadiums equipped with cooling systems. The risk of dangerous heat has nearly doubled since the 1994 US World Cup, prompting concerns for players and fans. **FIFA** is monitoring conditions and implementing contingency protocols to mitigate risks.

recent_articles.title: Warning of record global temperatures
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)** has issued a stark warning about the impending threat of record global temperatures, urging urgent action to mitigate climate change.  The report highlights the increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events, including heatwaves, droughts, and floods, as consequences of rising global temperatures.

recent_articles.title: Record global temperatures possible as chance of a 'super El NiÃ±o' grows - BBC Weather
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **NOAA**, **Bureau of Meteorology (BoM)**, and the **European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF)** have increased confidence that a strong El Niño event is developing in the tropical Pacific.  This could lead to record global temperatures, potentially surpassing 2.5C by autumn, with significant impacts on weather patterns worldwide. The consequences could include humanitarian crises due to reduced harvests and higher food prices.

recent_articles.title: GBA chief commissioner directs corporations to prepare for monsoon - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **M. Maheshwar Rao**, Chief Commissioner of the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA), has issued directives to city corporations regarding monsoon preparedness. **Rao** ordered parades of PRAHARI vehicles, inspections of tree-cutting equipment and emergency response systems, and detailed reports on preparedness from commissioners. He also emphasized joint inspections with railway officials for flood-prone areas, prioritization of dilapidated structure removal, and the procurement of litter pickers to enhance sanitation.

recent_articles.title: Lost beneath Sudan’s sands: Scientists discover 6,000-year-old massive monuments from a forgotten civilisation
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A satellite survey in Sudan's Atbai Desert has revealed 280 large stone burial monuments known as 'Atbai Enclosure Burials' (AEBs). Dating back to the Middle and Late Holocene, these structures were built between 4500 BCE and 2500 BCE by pastoral communities who adapted to the changing Sahara.  The AEBs demonstrate a society capable of organizing large communal efforts and planning skillfully, even in challenging conditions. The findings suggest that cattle played a central role in their lives and beliefs, with some sites containing both human and cattle burials.

recent_articles.title: Drop mall proposal in Koyambedu, develop green space instead: Anbumani - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Anbumani Ramadoss**, leader of the PMK, urged the **Tamil Nadu government** to develop a large urban green park instead of converting the existing Koyambedu bus terminus land into a commercial mall.  The **CMDA** reportedly proposed three options for the 36-acre site: an urban green park, a mixed-use commercial complex, and a shopping mall. Ramadoss argued that these commercial proposals would worsen environmental stress in the city and called on the government to merge the bus terminus land with the surrounding omni bus stand area to create a larger green space.

recent_articles.title: Brazil’s Atlantic forest records lowest deforestation in 40 years | Brazil | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Brazil’s Atlantic forest**, the country's most threatened biome, recorded its lowest level of deforestation since monitoring began in 1985, with **8,658 hectares** of deforestation in 2025. Environmentalists attribute this decline to a combination of public pressure, civil society mobilization, environmental policies and enforcement actions. However, the recent approval of the "devastation bill" in Brazil's congress, which weakens environmental law, poses a significant threat to this progress.  This legislation could lead to a return of deforestation levels seen under **Jair Bolsonaro**, who led the country to record-high deforestation rates during his 2019–2023 presidency.

recent_articles.title: Australia Lizard Population: Why Australia became home to one of the world’s largest lizard populations | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Australia's** long environmental history, including periods of climatic change and geographic isolation, has contributed to its high concentration of reptile species, particularly skinks.  The continent's gradual shifts between wetter and drier conditions allowed reptiles to adapt and evolve into distinct species over millions of years. This process was further enhanced by the continent's isolation from other landmasses, leading to the evolution of specialized ecological niches within diverse microhabitats. The resulting diversity is reflected in Australia's well over a thousand lizard species, with skinks forming one of the largest components of that diversity.

recent_articles.title: Rhode Island: 6 lakes larger than Rhode Island in the US: Lake Huron and Lake Michigan are nearly 15 times larger | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Lake Huron, Lake Michigan, Lake Ontario, Lake Erie, Lake Superior
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rhode Island**, despite being the smallest state in the US by area, is dwarfed by several freshwater lakes within North America.  Lakes like **Lake of the Woods**, **Lake Ontario**, **Lake Erie**, **Lake Michigan**, **Lake Huron**, and **Lake Superior** are significantly larger than Rhode Island, each boasting unique characteristics and ecological importance. These lakes, with their vast size and diverse wildlife, contribute to the remarkable freshwater geography of North America.

recent_articles.title: Bengaluru: Nearly 80% land acquisition done for PRR Package 1, work order to be issued in June - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Bengaluru Business Corridor Ltd. (BBC)**, a Special Purpose Vehicle formed to oversee the **Peripheral Ring Road (PRR)** project, is set to issue work orders for Package 1 between Tumakuru Road and Ballari Road in June. Civil works are anticipated to commence three months after that.  The first on-ground construction for the PRR, which has been delayed for over two decades, will begin with this package.

recent_articles.title: Typical English roast dinner potentially ‘drenched’ in 102 pesticides, says report | Pesticides | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Greenpeace** has released a report revealing that the traditional Sunday roast, often considered a rustic meal, may contain pesticides. The report found over 100 pesticides used on vegetables and fruits, including some banned in the EU due to health concerns. **Greenpeace UK**'s senior campaigner, Nina Schrank, stated that this widespread pesticide use is harming wildlife and ecosystems.  The UK government has a national action plan aimed at reducing pesticide use by 2030, while **Greenpeace** calls for stricter regulations and increased organic agriculture.

recent_articles.title: 24x7 control rooms for disaster management to be set up in Ernakulam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **District Collector G. Priyanka** announced the activation of **Taluk Emergency Operation Centres (TEOCs)** by May 20th to prepare for the monsoon season. The district has received a ₹5 crore disaster relief fund from the **State Disaster Management Authority (SDMA)** and additional funds for desilting rivers, cleaning canals, and installing geobags along the Chellanam coast.  Local bodies have been tasked with identifying potential relief camps and furnishing equipment for emergency response.

recent_articles.title: Nicobarese oppose proposal for three wildlife sanctuaries - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Tribal Council of Little and Great Nicobar
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union government** notified three wildlife sanctuaries in the Little Nicobar, Menchal, and Meroe islands in 2022, despite concerns from the **Tribal Council of Little and Great Nicobar** that the process was not conducted with proper consultation. The council argues that these islands are culturally and spiritually significant to them and their traditional practices should be respected.  Congress leader and former Environment Minister **Jairam Ramesh** has written to Tribal Affairs Minister **Jual Oram**, urging him to intervene and withdraw clearances granted under the Forest Rights Act for the Great Nicobar Island project, citing violations of the law. The **Tribal Council** has consistently objected to the sanctuaries' declaration, arguing that it encroaches on their pre-existing rights and will negatively impact their livelihoods.  The Calcutta High Court has dismissed preliminary objections raised by the government in relation to the Forest Rights Act violation allegations.

recent_articles.title: 27-year-old Indian man killed in rare bear attack in Canada; last fatal incident reported 6 years ago - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A 27-year-old Indian man died after being attacked by a black bear at a uranium exploration site in Saskatchewan, Canada. The incident occurred near Nordbye Lake on Friday evening while the man was working for **UraniumX Discovery Corp.**  The company assisted workers at the scene and provided equipment and supplies. A civilian present shot and killed the bear following the attack. **Douglas Clark**, a professor at the University of Saskatchewan’s School of Environment and Sustainability, stated that fatal bear attacks in Saskatchewan are extremely rare.

recent_articles.title: Magnus the wandering walrus leaves Scotland for Norway | Animals | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Magnus**, a young male walrus who became a local celebrity in Scotland after traveling 200 miles south from the Arctic, has been spotted in Norway. **Åge Jakobsen**, a local birdwatcher, reported seeing Magnus on a floating dock in Buerholmen at Hidra.  The walrus' journey across the North Sea was monitored by British Divers Marine Life Rescue, who noted that adolescent walruses often wander beyond their usual range. This sighting is considered rare and likely due to climate change affecting their Arctic habitat.

recent_articles.title: Gaza sisters win prize for turning rubble into reusable bricks
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Farah** and **Tala Mousa**, two teenage sisters from Gaza, won the Earth Prize for their innovative use of rubble to create reusable bricks. The sisters, displaced after their home was bombed, developed the blocks as a solution to the destruction caused by the war in Gaza. They plan to use their $12,500 prize to train young people to produce the bricks and contribute to the reconstruction effort.  The Earth Prize is an environmental award that recognizes solutions to global challenges.

recent_articles.title: Heavy rain, hailstorm lash Lahore, inundating low-lying areas - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rain and hailstorms caused flooding in several areas of Lahore on Wednesday, prompting the **Pakistan Meteorological Department** to issue a warning for upper parts of the country. The **Lahore Water and Sanitation Agency (WASA)** recorded rainfall totals ranging from 11.2mm to 95mm across various locations, with Lakshmi Chowk receiving the highest amount.  The **Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA)** urged citizens to take precautions and avoid unnecessary travel, while directing district administrations to ensure efficient drainage of rainwater. The **WASA** deployed emergency teams and directed all disposal stations to remain operational.

recent_articles.title: Forest secrets: Lost medieval town missing for 600 years finally found beneath a forest in Poland | - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Researchers** from the **Relicta Foundation**, a Polish archaeological group, have uncovered the remains of Stolzenberg, a medieval town that disappeared centuries ago.  The site, located in northwestern Poland, was identified through historical records and non-invasive surveys. The team discovered defensive earthworks, street patterns, and hundreds of artifacts, including silver coins and belt fittings, dating back to the Middle Ages. **Poland’s Ministry of Culture and National Heritage** supported the research, which has provided valuable insights into medieval town planning and abandonment in frontier regions.

recent_articles.title: Prolonged power outage plunges Thripunithura and nearby areas into darkness - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Heavy rain and wind caused a prolonged power outage in several areas of Thripunithura, Kerala on Tuesday.  **Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB)** officials reported that over 80 transformers were disrupted, with damage to more than 60 electric poles across the affected regions. **The KSEB** stated that power supply was restored to most areas by Wednesday evening, but some residents faced difficulties due to lack of backup power and continued disruptions in certain locations.

recent_articles.title: Official marking of land for Brazil’s uncontacted Kawahiva people begins after 27-year wait | Brazil | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Brazilian** government has begun the demarcation of the 410,000-hectare Pardo River Kawahiva Indigenous territory in Mato Grosso and Amazonas states. This decision comes after 27 years of efforts to protect the uncontacted people living there, with support from organizations like the **National Indigenous Peoples’ Foundation** (Funai) and campaigners.  However, legal challenges from groups linked to agribusiness have delayed progress, highlighting ongoing threats to the Kawahiva's survival. Despite these obstacles, Funai is planning buffer zones to protect the territory from deforestation and advocates for increased resources to ensure the safety of isolated Indigenous peoples.

recent_articles.title: Series of tremors near Tehran renews concerns over major quake risk | Earthquakes News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Iran** experienced a series of nine small earthquakes near Tehran overnight, renewing concerns about the potential for a major seismic event. The tremors occurred near the Mosha fault, one of the country's most active seismic zones, and were felt in an area close to the capital.  Seismologist Mehdi Zare warned that while the recent activity may not indicate a future earthquake, Tehran's vulnerability due to its dense urban development and proximity to active faults remains a significant concern.

recent_articles.title: Summer showers, strong winds lash district - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Strong summer showers** with accompanying **strong winds** caused widespread damage across the district on Tuesday evening, May 12, 2026.  Ten houses sustained damage in various taluks, including Kothamangalam, Muvattupuzha, Kochi, and Thripunithura. Tree branches fell on vehicles and disrupted traffic, while a roof collapse at an automobile company building caused further damage. **Fire and Rescue Services** cleared fallen trees and restored traffic flow.  Authorities warned of continued strong summer showers in the coming days.

recent_articles.title: Elephant dies after fall near Nadugani ghat road - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A young female elephant died after falling from a steep cliff near Nilambur, India.  **Forest officials** confirmed the presence of fresh tiger pugmarks near the carcass, but concluded that the elephant's death was likely caused by the fall itself. The elephant's trunk had been partially eaten by a tiger after it died two days prior. **Forest officials** moved the carcass to a convenient location and buried it.

recent_articles.title: Labour must fulfil promise to introduce clean air act, charities urge | Air pollution | The Guardian
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Over 60 charities have urged **Ministers** to introduce a new clean air act that would ban wood burning, clear diesel vehicles from the roads, and force councils to reduce pollution. The call comes after the government has made no move to reinstate a proposed clean air act dropped from its election manifesto in 2023.  The charities point out that dirty air is costing the country billions of pounds annually and harming public health. They also criticize the government for failing to enforce existing regulations against wood burning despite thousands of complaints, while acknowledging efforts by the Scottish government to address concerns about rural communities' reliance on wood-burning stoves.

recent_articles.title: Work on 1.1 MLD sewage treatment plant at Edakochi expected to be completed by August - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kochi Corporation** is nearing completion of a 1.1 MLD sewage treatment plant (STP) in Edakochi, Division 16, with work expected to be finished by August. The project, funded under the **Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT)** Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) program, aims to treat wastewater from approximately 2,000 households.  The system includes a household-level collection network, conveyance system, and treatment unit, with a total length of 17.9 km of sewage pipeline being laid within the division. Tidal flooding has posed challenges to the project's progress.

recent_articles.title: Mount Dukono: I led hikers up an Indonesian volcano - and then it erupted
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A guide who led a group of hikers up Mount Dukono in Indonesia has described the harrowing moment they were caught in the eruption that killed three people. **Reza Selang**, who runs a tour company, said he was unaware of the climbing prohibition and warnings issued by authorities about the volcano's activity.  The Indonesian government has closed all entrances to the mountain and is investigating possible negligence by tourism operators or individuals. The surviving hikers were evacuated from the mountain, while the bodies of two Singaporean hikers and an Indonesian hiker have been recovered.

recent_articles.title: WRD stops release of water from Sathanur dam in Tiruvannamalai for irrigation - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Water Resources Department (WRD)** has halted water releases from the Sathanur dam due to a significant drop in water levels. The decision affects 50,000 acres of farmland in Tiruvannamalai, Kallakuruchi, and Villupuram districts, impacting farmers who relied on the dam's irrigation canals for their crops.  The WRD stated that the dam currently has only 18% of its capacity remaining, insufficient to support irrigation needs or domestic consumption.

recent_articles.title: Scientists discover massive ancient ship graveyard with 150 hidden shipwrecks beneath Gibraltar waters | - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Archaeologists** from the **University of Cádiz** and **University of Granada** have uncovered a vast underwater archaeological concentration in the Bay of Gibraltar, potentially one of the largest in the western Mediterranean.  The three-year project, known as Project Herakles, documented over 150 sites, most dating back to ancient civilizations and spanning multiple centuries. The discoveries include ancient Phoenician and Punic vessels, Roman-era ships, medieval wrecks, and military vessels from the 18th, 19th, and 20th centuries. Researchers are using digital technology to preserve these historical remains for future generations.

recent_articles.title: Four cheetah cubs die at Kuno in suspected leopard attack - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Four** cheetah cubs, born in April and the first to be born in the open forest since India's reintroduction program began in 2022, were found dead on Tuesday (May 12, 2026) in **Kuno National Park**, Madhya Pradesh.  The carcasses of the one-month-old cubs were partially eaten and marks of a leopard attack were found during post-mortem examinations. The mother cheetah is safe and healthy, according to officials. A thorough investigation is underway into the incident, which highlights the challenges of adapting cheetahs to their natural habitat.

recent_articles.title: World Deadliest Snakes: King Cobra Capitals: 10 countries where the world’s deadliest snake thrives | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **King cobras**, the world's longest venomous snake, inhabit forests and wetlands across South and Southeast Asia.  Top countries with significant populations include India, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Nepal, Vietnam, Cambodia, and China. These countries support diverse king cobra habitats, which are threatened by habitat loss, deforestation, and poaching.  Conservation efforts focus on protecting forest corridors and educating communities about safe coexistence with these fascinating creatures.

recent_articles.title: Longest Rivers In The World: Exploring the 9 longest rivers in the world, from the Nile to the Congo | World News - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The U.S. Geological Survey**, **Guinness World Records**, and scientists have been debating the length of various rivers, particularly the Nile River and the Amazon River. Other notable rivers include the Yangtze, Missouri-Mississippi system, Yenisey River, Yellow River, Ob-Irtysh system, Rio de la Plata, and Congo River.  These rivers play a vital role in shaping landscapes, supporting ecosystems, and influencing human civilization.

recent_articles.title: Two killed in elephant attacks in The Nilgiris - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Two people** died in separate elephant attacks in the Nilgiris region of India. **B.S. Rajappan**, a temple priest, was killed while returning home from a temple near Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, and **C. Raghu**, who was walking with friends after a festival, was also killed by an elephant in Konavakarai. recent_articles.title: ‘Whole morning revolves around gas’: Pakistan’s fuel crisis enters kitchens | Women News | Al Jazeera

recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Scientists** have been studying the origins of Earth's building blocks, particularly through the analysis of meteorites and isotopic compositions.  These studies suggest that **carbonaceous chondrites**, considered primitive materials from the outer solar system, played a significant role in providing carbon, water, and volatile elements necessary for life on Earth. Isotopic fingerprints found in Earth's mantle, such as those of molybdenum, indicate genetic links between Earth and these meteorites, suggesting a common source for both.  This research challenges the traditional view that comets were solely responsible for delivering water to Earth.  Further investigation into this process will provide more insight into the origins of life and planetary formation within our solar system.
